feature: A cross fade plays in the editor the way it looks in the export
summary: Two causes of a dissolve showing the wrong frame while it plays are fixed. A frame the dissolve borrows from past a clip's end is now stood in for by the nearest borrowed frame, not by one from back inside the clip, which could be a second old. And a play pass is no longer started over when a restart would decode from the same key frame. Playing right after a scrub that lands far past a key frame still holds a slightly old frame for about half a second; that part is still open.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Any screen recording of yours works; the walk that measures it is a-cross-fade-plays-as-exported-walk (full-screen Retina fixture, key frames two seconds apart).

try.do: Open a long screen recording, drag a second recording onto V1 so it overlaps the end of the first, and pick the place where they meet.
Put a Cross dissolve on that join from the transition picker.
Click the ruler about a second before the dissolve, wait a moment, and press Space. Watch the dissolve.
Play it again at 0.5x and at 2x from the speed menu beside play.
Drag the playhead quickly onto a spot just before the dissolve, let go, and press Space at once.
Export the edit as an MP4 and play the same stretch in the file beside the editor.

evaluate: Does the dissolve in the editor now look like the one in the exported file, with nothing blinking off and on?
After the quick drag and an immediate Space, is the half second where the picture holds a slightly old frame noticeable to you?
If you still see the flicker, which transition and which recordings was it, so the walk can be pointed at that exact shape?
rough: What I could and could not reproduce: playing a dissolve from rest (1x, 0.5x, 2x, from its first frame) matched the export frame for frame on this Mac, on the fixture and on two of your own HEVC screen recordings, even with 14 of 16 cores busy. The failure that reproduced every time was playing right after a scrub: the old build drew a frame up to 34 frames (about a second) old for both sides of the dissolve; your recording showed a screenshot thumbnail in the corner that the right frame no longer has.

Cause 1, the flicker: a frame a dissolve borrows from past a clip's end (or before its start) that was not read yet was stood in for by a frame from back inside the clip, then the next borrowed frame jumped forward again. The export never shows stand-ins, so it was clean. Now the nearest borrowed frame stands in. A unit test fails on the old code and passes now.

Cause 2: a play pass that fell four frames behind was started over at the playhead, but on a screen recording (key frames about 2 seconds apart) the new pass decodes from the same key frame, so every restart threw the work away and none ever handed over a frame. Now it is kept when no key frame lies between, and frames the playhead has already passed are decoded but not turned into pictures.

Still open, and why the task stays open: pressing Space right after a scrub that lands about a second past a key frame needs about 0.6s to decode the first frame (measured 614ms on your 3456x2234 HEVC recording), and starting play cancels the read that was already decoding there. After the fix the frame held is a tenth of a second old instead of a second, but it is still held. Fixing it means play waits for its first frame or takes over the resting read; that is the next step on this task.

Pictures of your own recordings are not in this public repo. The before and after pair, and the readings, are in ~/Library/Caches/Photonz Cross Fade Evidence on this Mac. The reel here (2026-11-20-cross-fade-reel.mp4, canvas left, export right, 0.5x through the two-clip dissolve) and the sheets use the repo's fixture.
No mock covers this; it is playback correctness, nothing on screen moved.
